title: The printing press was never invented
premise: In 1440 Gutenberg's metal movable type fails in the workshop and is not taken up elsewhere. Books and notices remain copied by hand, costly and few, so reading stays the skill of scribes, clerks and merchants' households. News, law and craft knowledge travel by voice, memory and painted images, slowing standardization and large-scale coordination.

chain.event: Gutenberg's Mainz workshop runs out of money after failed trials with movable metal type and his backers withdraw support.
chain.consequence: No workable press is demonstrated, other craftsmen do not copy the method, and book production remains entirely by hand.

chain.event: Rulers, town councils and universities expand rooms of hand copyists to meet demand for law codes, textbooks and merchants' letters.
chain.consequence: Books stay costly and rare, schooling stays limited to clerks, scribes and merchants' households, and fewer than one person in ten can read.

chain.event: Students of nature share results only through handwritten letters and live demonstrations, recopied with slips and delays.
chain.consequence: Diagrams, tables and machine plans take decades to become standard, so tools, mills and instruments remain local in design and slow to improve.

chain.event: Mill owners and early rail lines train workers by long apprenticeship and spoken orders because no cheap printed manuals, tickets or timetables exist.
chain.consequence: Firms stay small, parts stay fitted by hand, and towns add low housing near yards rather than large suburbs linked by paper-managed transport.

chain.event: Merchants and town councils pay for wired voice lines and later wireless voice boxes to share prices and news without printed sheets.
chain.consequence: Public criers, dictation offices and group listening rooms become the main news system, and painted picture signs replace printed notices in streets.

chain.event: Makers perfect sound recorders, picture transmitters and voice telephones while office work still depends on spoken dictation and hand-ledgers.
chain.consequence: Administration stays labor-heavy with large staffs for copying and memorizing, coordination by voice keeps organizations mid-sized, and literacy remains uncommon through 2026.

eras.caption: 1526 · Hand-copied signs and low workshops
eras.visualPrompt: Transform this scene to 1526 in a world where the printing press was never invented. Low street houses in the region's own building tradition hold daylight copying rooms, with large painted picture walls, hand-lettered boards and criers' platforms and no printed paper.
eras.visualPromptIndoor: A long daylight copying room in the region's own building tradition with rows of desks, ink pots, parchment sheets and picture charts, scribes writing and reciting aloud.

differences: low two- to three-storey street houses with large daylight copying rooms instead of taller merchant houses with print shops (because books are made by teams of scribes needing window light and low benches)
large hand-painted picture walls and carved shop marks instead of printed posters and playbills (because news must be seen as images when few can read multiplied texts)
mounted letter carriers, pack horses and handcarts with parchment bundles instead of heavy wagons with bales of printed paper (because each copy is costly and moves in small guarded lots)
cobbled lanes with speaking platforms and reading benches instead of streets lined with posted paper notices (because laws and prices are announced aloud by criers)
inner-plot drying yards and small vellum stores instead of large paper-mill yards and storehouses (because skins and limited rag paper come from small local makers)
kept: the region's own building tradition in walls and roofs

eras.caption: 1926 · Painted walls, low blocks, few motors
eras.visualPrompt: Transform this scene to 1926 in a world where the printing press was never invented. Mid-rise blocks in the region's own building tradition line streets with painted murals and hand-lettered boards, horse trams and bicycles passing under simple lamps with no printed signs or cars.
eras.visualPromptIndoor: A group listening room in the region's own building tradition with long benches, a central voice box, hand-written ledgers on shelves and large picture charts on the walls.

differences: three- to four-storey street blocks with courtyards instead of six- to ten-storey office and apartment blocks (because voice orders and hand ledgers keep firms mid-sized and limit capital pooling)

horse trams, bicycles, handcarts and few shared motor vans instead of mass private cars and motor buses (because driving and repair skills pass only by long apprenticeship and parts networks stay thin)
large painted murals and hand-lettered price boards instead of printed billboards and newsstands (because advertising must work as pictures and speech for a largely non-reading public)

mild gas lamps and few wired bulbs on main streets instead of bright citywide electric lighting with signal systems (because power planning without cheap duplicated plans stays limited to central lines)
compact town quarters with gardens, orchards and stable yards between homes instead of wide commuter suburbs with filling stations (because daily life stays on foot and near work)
kept: mature street trees and seasonal climate
the region's own building tradition in facades and roofs

eras.caption: 2026 · Picture walls and courtyard blocks
eras.visualPrompt: Transform this scene to 2026 in a world where the printing press was never invented. Mid-rise courtyard blocks in the region's own building tradition with hand-painted picture walls and chalk boards, trams, bicycles and speaker poles in planted streets with no cars or printed signs.
eras.visualPromptIndoor: A dictation hall in the region's own building tradition with rows of desks, voice horns, hand-kept ledgers and large instructional pictures, clerks speaking and copying by daylight.

differences: four- to six-storey courtyard blocks instead of glass high-rise towers (because voice-led offices with hand records favor mid-size firms and mid-rise streets)
street trams, bicycles, handcarts and shared motor vans instead of dense private car traffic (because mechanic skills spread slowly by apprenticeship and fleets stay small and local)
hand-painted picture walls, carved marks and chalk price boards instead of printed signs, glowing billboards and paper posters (because messages must work as images and speech when reading is rare)

stone-set lanes and packed-earth sidestreets with speaker poles and listening shelters instead of wide asphalt arterials with sign gantries (because public news arrives by announced voice and scheduled readings)
market gardens, fruit trees and stable yards between houses instead of parking lots and fuel courts (because food and draft animals remain close to town centers)
kept: the region's own building tradition in walls and roofs

eras.caption: 2126 · A city that speaks in pictures
eras.visualPrompt: Transform this scene to 2126 in a world where the printing press was never invented. Buildings in the region's own building tradition are covered from street to roof in huge painted murals and carved picture reliefs telling stories in images, with bell and speaker towers at street corners and slow trams, and no written words anywhere.
eras.visualPromptIndoor: This room in 2126 without printing: walls painted with picture stories, a carved image panel, a listening horn instead of shelves of books.

differences: whole facades painted with picture stories and carved image reliefs instead of signs and billboards with text (because few people read and messages are pictures)
tall bell and speaker towers at street corners instead of screens (because news and orders are spoken aloud)
five-storey courtyard blocks instead of office towers (because firms stay small without printed paperwork)
slow trams and bicycles instead of heavy car traffic (because mass production and manuals came late)
absent: written words or letters on buildings

eras.caption: 3026 · Story facades of stone and coloured glass
eras.visualPrompt: Transform this scene to 3026 in a world where the printing press was never invented. Buildings in the region's own building tradition carry a thousand years of carved stone stories and great coloured-glass picture windows, mellowed by time and framed by trees and gardens; footpaths and small trams, no writing anywhere.
eras.visualPromptIndoor: This room in 3026 without printing: a carved story panel, light through a coloured-glass picture window, plants along the sill.

differences: facades of carved stone story panels and coloured-glass picture windows instead of plain walls with signage (because a millennium of memory is kept in images)
low courtyard buildings among trees instead of towers (because the city grew slowly and was kept)
footpaths and small trams instead of roads (because daily life stays local)
